messages:
incident-bot: PAGER DUTY: pg-primary-db: connection-pool-exhausted (P1) — page routed to oncall@eng-oncall. Trigger: pgbouncer max_client_connections exceeded, latency spike > 1200ms.
pagerduty-bot: Pager: pg-primary-db | Service: postgres-main | Severity: P1 | Escalation: oncall-sre -> kevin | Details: 503s observed on /api/generate, 400+ errors/min.
kevin: acked. I'm on it, joining console now. :headphones:
maria: seeing steady 500s from web-prod -> db, elevated wait_timeout on pgbouncer. Any recent deploys?
kevin: no deploys in last 45m. Metrics: pgbouncer-cluster: cl_active=1024, cl_waiting=98, max_clients=1024. Looks like we hit acceptqueue.
sanjay: i'm pulling pgbouncer and postgres stats. running `psql -h pg-primary -c "SELECT pid, state, query_start, query FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE state='active' ORDER BY query_start DESC LIMIT 20;"`
kevin: logs show a batch job from analytics-service spiking connections — multiple long-running COPY/INSERTs. Query examples: `COPY analytics_events FROM stdin;` open for >10m.
maria: customer impact: partial write failures and elevated latency on any endpoint that depends on write-confirmation. Could be read-only endpoints ok for some users. SLOs impacted for 12 customers (notifying CS).
alice: adding mitigation steps: 1) throttle analytics-service traffic at LB layer, 2) move analytics job to replica or pause, 3) increase pgbouncer max_clients temporarily, 4) start pg-replica promotion fallback if primary degrades.
kevin: doing LB throttle now — applied rate-limit = 50 r/s to analytics-service via envoy. Confirming connections are dropping.
sanjay: pgbouncer stats after throttle: cl_active=810, cl_waiting=12, cl_cache=100, recent auth_failures=0. Good.
maria: running `SELECT pg_terminate_backend(pid) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE query LIKE 'COPY analytics_events%' AND state='active';` to free stuck backfills. Proceed?\e:kevin: yes, terminate them but keep one for stateful resume. Be careful.
kevin: terminated 6 long-running COPYs. Active connections reduced. Watching error rate on prod.
alice: edge case: if we free too many connections instantly, API traffic may surge and hit connection limit again. Consider graceful drain: `pg_terminate_backend` + slow-unpause analytics.
kevin: error rate down from 420 errors/min -> 38 errors/min in 5m. latency 95th went from 1200ms -> 240ms. Looks stable.
maria: CS update drafted: "Partial write errors observed due to DB connection saturation from internal analytics job. Mitigations applied; most services recovered. Customers with ongoing writes may have seen 503s between 19:02-19:10 UTC. Root cause under investigation." Anyone want to send?
sanjay: i'll send the CS blurb and raise a post-incident action item to move analytics job to replica + add circuit-breaker in the job runner.
kevin: handing off to sanjay for postmortem and rollback monitoring. I will stay available for 15m.
sanjay: taking over the thread. I'll run a health-check script every 5m and keep the rate-limit until next deployment. Creating ticket: ORG-4351 (pg conn saturation mitigation + pgbouncer sizing).
incident-bot: NOTE: Pager closed automatically after 00:38:23 of active paging (ack by kevin).
alice: retrospective notes inline: - need per-service connection caps at pgbouncer auth_user level - require backfill job to use replica credentials by default - add analytic job circuit-breaker + retry/backoff.
maria: closing loop: double-checking replication lag and WAL shipping after we terminated COPYs. replication_lag < 2s. Good.
kevin: summary: cause = analytics backfill opening too many DB connections -> pgbouncer acceptqueue fill -> client 503s. Mitigation = LB throttle + terminate long-running COPYs + temporary pgbouncer headroom increase. Next steps: postmortem + config changes (ORG-4351).
sanjay: update: leaving rate-limit on for 30m, monitoring dashboard pinned. Handing back to kevin if needed.
kevin: thanks — closing pager. :white_check_mark:
